//: Every field De-Sentry v2 reads, with its default. The desktop app writes this file for you -- you are not expected to hand-edit it, and the app is the single point of access. It stays human-readable anyway, because a config you cannot read during an incident is a config you cannot debug.
//supervisor: An app-local control-plane node: hardware discovery, node lifecycle, key custody, quorum-gated ledger checkpointing. Never elected, never holds replicated data, never on the write path. Its api_bind_addr is forced to loopback.
//quota_mb: Total on-disk budget for this node in MiB. 0 means unlimited. Enforced in StorageEngine::PutRaw and again inside each router backend.
//quota_split: How that budget is divided between subsystems, as percentages summing to 100. The AI sizing step proposes a split per workload shape: vector workloads shift +15 into cache_hash, time-series workloads shift +10 into ledger.
//engines: Router backends this node may bind collections to. Always available: kv, columnar_lite, ts_rollup, vector_hnsw_lite, graph_adj. Available only when vendored and compiled in: sqlite, duckdb, lmdb, sqlite_vec (see third_party/README.md; check GET /_engines on a running node).
//replication_factor: Replicas per key on the consistent-hash ring. 3 is the default.
//transit_ttl_seconds: How long bytes held for an offline owner survive before expiring. 0 disables expiry, which is an operational decision rather than a default -- the node logs a warning if you set it.
//retention_days: Default time-series retention for collections that do not set their own. 0 keeps everything.
//encrypt_at_rest: At-rest AES-GCM encryption. The key never appears in this file: keychain_ref names an entry in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service) that the app unlocks and hands to the process.
//max_peer_threads: Worker threads for eager broadcast fan-out. Bounded so a write to a 50-node mesh does not spawn 50 threads.
//peer_rate_limit: Token-bucket admission control on inbound P2P requests, per authenticated peer. 0 disables it -- do not run that configuration on an untrusted network.
